title: Annotatio III §.VI (1): Reformed at Leipzig ready to subscribe the Invariata — Variata not rejected; Nauenburg 1561 precedent; Brandenburg/Hessian Relation confession
pass_a_gloss: (1) That under the very beginning the Reformed Theologians did not hesitate to addict themselves to the Unaltered Augsburg Confession, being most ready also to subscribe the same whenever the other party should desire that, the Variata or Philippica meanwhile not rejected or repudiated, but defended in that manner in which the Estates of the Empire in the Nauenburg Convention in the year 1561 had judged that this same one also ought to be admitted. Since we have already remembered this deed of the Leipzig Reformers several times, it will help in this place to bring into the midst their words making for this, from the German Relation concerning the Leipzig Colloquy.
pass_b_english: (1) Right at the start the Reformed theologians did not hesitate to bind themselves to the Unaltered Augsburg Confession, and were fully ready to subscribe it whenever the other side asked — without rejecting or repudiating the Variata (Philippica), which they defended as the Imperial Estates had admitted it at the Nauenburg Convention in 1561.
Since this Leipzig Reformed act has been remembered before, it helps to bring in their own words from the German Relation of the Leipzig Colloquy.

There the Brandenburg and Hessian theologians voluntarily confessed with mouth and heart the 1530 Confession delivered to Charles V at Augsburg, and said they would subscribe it — even the Saxon Elector’s exemplar in the Augapfel — whenever and wherever asked, because they and their lords already bound themselves to it in church and school.
source_text: (1) Quòd sub ipsum initium Reformati Theologi, Confessioni Augustanae Invariatae sese addicere nulli dubitarunt, paratissimi etiam subscribere eidem, quandocunque istud altera pars desideraret, non rejectâ interim aut repudiata Variata, seu Philippicâ, defensâ verò eô modô, quô Status Imperii in Conventu Nauenburgico An. 1561. hanc quoque ipsam admittendam duxerant. Cum hujus Reformatorum Lipsiensium facti jam aliquoties meminerimus, juvabit hôc locô verba eorum huc facientia in medium adducere, ex Relatione de Colloquio Lipsiaco, germanica.
notes: Lipsiacum (1): Invariata subscription readiness; Variata/Nauenburg; German Relation paraphrase.
